tldr: AtomAgents is a physics-aware multi-modal multi-agent AI framework that uses LLM-powered agents collaborating autonomously to design and analyze metallic alloys through atomistic simulations, knowledge retrieval, and multi-modal data integration, significantly reducing human intervention.
contributions: Integrating physics-based simulations (LAMMPS MD) with generative AI (LLMs) for crystalline materials design
Multi-modal data integration across simulations, experiments, databases, and theoretical models
Advanced simulation capabilities for retrieving new physics through atomistic simulations
Reduction in human intervention through autonomous workflow design for high-throughput simulations
Accessibility for non-expert researchers via textual input interfaces
Full interpretability with traceable agent-tool interactions
methods: AtomAgents employs a multi-agent system where core agents (User, Engineer, Scientist, Group Manager) collaborate dynamically, calling specialized tools powered by GPT-family LLMs accessed via the OpenAI API. Each tool (planning, computation, knowledge retrieval, plot analysis, coding) contains its own set of agents with distinct profiles. Planning is handled by Admin, Planner, and Critic agents. Atomistic simulations are performed using LAMMPS at zero temperature, with pre-written LAMMPS scripts integrated as Python functions. The system perceives multi-modal data, reasons and plans, then acts through tool execution in an iterative loop.
results: Experiment I demonstrated automated computation and retrieval of material properties (lattice constants, elastic constants C11/C12/C44, and surface energies for [110] and [111] planes of Al and Ni), with results saved to CSV and agreement confirmed between computed and Mishin paper reported values. Experiment II modeled screw dislocations in BCC materials. The framework successfully designed metallic alloys with enhanced properties compared to pure counterparts and highlighted the crucial role of solid solution alloying in steering advanced metallic alloy development.
limitations: Current state-of-the-art LLMs show weak performance in constructing LAMMPS scripts, requiring human-generated scripts instead of autonomous script generation
LLMs face limitations including inability to perform physics-based simulations natively, restricted access to external sources, and reliance on potentially outdated knowledge
Simulations are performed only at zero temperature
